question: What is the primary function of the rectum during elimination?

options.A: Temporary storage reservoir for fecal matter
options.B: Major site of water and electrolyte absorption
options.C: Production of digestive enzymes for waste breakdown
options.D: Secretion of mucus to lubricate the anal canal

explanation: The rectum holds waste until elimination occurs, expanding to trigger stretch receptors when full. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T13#GNS121_U1_T13_h1)

question: Mass movements in the colon are typically triggered by which physiological event?
explanation: Eating stimulates the gastrocolic reflex, which initiates powerful mass movements to push fecal contents toward the rectum. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T13#GNS121_U1_T13_h1)

question: Which spinal cord segments mediate the parasympathetic defecation reflex?
explanation: The sacral segments S2 to S4 contain the parasympathetic outflow that controls the lower bowel and pelvic organs. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T13#GNS121_U1_T13_h2)

question: Why is the intrinsic defecation reflex alone often insufficient for complete evacuation?

options.A: It only functions when the external sphincter is completely paralyzed
options.B: It prevents the relaxation of the internal anal sphincter
options.C: It relies entirely on voluntary skeletal muscle contractions
options.D: It produces weak peristaltic waves that need parasympathetic reinforcement

explanation: The local myenteric reflex creates mild pressure, requiring the spinal parasympathetic reflex to generate strong propulsive forces. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T13#GNS121_U1_T13_h2)

question: What type of muscle makes up the internal anal sphincter?
explanation: The internal anal sphincter consists of involuntary smooth muscle fibers that maintain continuous resting tone. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T13#GNS121_U1_T13_h3)

question: Which nerve provides voluntary control to the external anal sphincter?
explanation: The pudendal nerve delivers somatic motor signals allowing conscious contraction or relaxation of the external sphincter. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T13#GNS121_U1_T13_h3)

question: A patient with severe cardiovascular disease is instructed to avoid straining during bowel movements because the Valsalva maneuver causes what immediate effect?

options.A: Sudden changes in blood pressure and heart rate
options.C: Complete relaxation of the internal sphincter
options.D: Immediate paralysis of the external anal sphincter

explanation: Straining via the Valsalva maneuver spikes intrathoracic pressure, drastically altering venous return and cardiac output, which stresses compromised hearts. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T13#GNS121_U1_T13_h4)

question: What action defines the initiation of the Valsalva maneuver?

options.A: Taking shallow breaths while walking around
options.B: Closing the glottis and contracting abdominal muscles
options.C: Stimulating the vagus nerve with cold water
options.D: Relaxing the diaphragm completely during expiration

explanation: The maneuver relies on a closed glottis and forceful abdominal wall contraction to generate high intra-abdominal pressure. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T13#GNS121_U1_T13_h4)

question: A patient with fecal impaction suddenly begins leaking small amounts of liquid stool. What is the physiological explanation for this?

options.A: Liquid stool from higher in the colon seeps around the impacted mass
options.B: Parasympathetic stimulation has accelerated total transit time
options.C: The liver is producing excess bile that liquefies all bowel contents
options.D: The internal anal sphincter has completely lost its smooth muscle tone

explanation: Liquid feces passing down from the proximal colon leak past the blockage, misleadingly presenting as diarrhea. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T13#GNS121_U1_T13_h5)

question: Which factor is a frequent behavioral cause of chronic constipation?

options.A: Excessive stimulation of the parasympathetic nerves
options.B: Voluntary suppression of the defecation reflex
options.C: High consumption of raw dietary fiber
options.D: Frequent performance of the Valsalva maneuver

explanation: Consistently ignoring the urge to defecate desensitizes rectal stretch receptors, leading to retained and hardened stool. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T13#GNS121_U1_T13_h5)
